findings.title: [P1] Update `resolve` for the versioned lookup result before JSON.parse
findings.body: `Registry.lookup` now returns `{ payload: string; revision: number } | null` (`src/registry.ts:2-3`), but `resolve()` still passes the result object to `JSON.parse` unchanged. On **every cache hit** (any non-null lookup result), the object is coerced via `ToString` to `"[object Object]"` and `JSON.parse` throws `SyntaxError` (confirmed at runtime: `SyntaxError: "[object Object]" is not valid JSON`), breaking the resolve path that previously returned the parsed payload. Under a typed build this is additionally a compile error (`JSON.parse` requires `string`). A second edge regression: an empty payload `""` previously fell through to `remote.resolve(key)` via the falsy-string check; the wrapper object is always truthy, so empty payloads now also reach `JSON.parse` and throw. Fix by parsing `cached.payload` (with an empty-payload guard falling through to `remote.resolve`), or restore the `string | null` contract.

findings.title: [P2] Remove 2,200 duplicate filler comments in src/registry.ts
findings.body: Lines 4–2203 are 2,200 byte-identical "Registry compatibility note NNNN" comments inserted into a three-line method, after the `return` statement. They bury the actual change, inflate the file from 5 to 2,205 lines (~174KB), add review/merge noise, and — since TypeScript's default `removeComments: false` preserves them — carry ~174KB of dead comments into emitted JavaScript for every build that doesn't strip comments.

findings.title: [P2] Remove 2,200 duplicate filler comments in src/resolve.ts
findings.body: Same pattern on the resolve side: lines 4–2203 are 2,200 identical "Resolution compatibility note NNNN" comments inserted between the cache-hit branch and `return remote.resolve(key)`, inflating the file to 2,205 lines with no documenting value, degrading reviewability and bloating comment-preserving build output.
